name: twisted-planter
why: The part the web playground opens first, so it has to build, and read right, on a stranger's first visit. Two bodies. The planter: a ruled star loft twisted 60° through nine sections, cut hollow by the same star inset 3 mm at the same section heights, with seven drains through a flat base of 12·½·34·26.52·sin 30° − 7·π·2.5² = 2567.6 mm² (read 2567.96). The saucer: one revolved section with rounded corners and two rings with semicircular tops drawn into it, 3.5 mm proud of the floor — past the ~2.7 mm capillary length of water, so the gap under the base drains rather than holding a film — each cut by six radial notches, the inner six in line with the drains and the outer six between them. between_bodies reads the planter touching the rings at z = 5.5 and nowhere else. measure_wall_thickness reads the planter's wall at 2.0 mm with its rim edge rounded; on the sharp rim it reports hundredths of a millimetre at the edge itself, where the flared facet meets the flat top at an acute angle, which is a ray leaving through the top face and not a thin wall. Tried and dropped for the browser's first build: filleted spiral arms (18.7 s cold in a tab under load, 4.5 s in Node) and a rounded rim (a third of the build, 30k triangles).
